correctness.rationale: For F=s h, direct differentiation gives J=(h,s h_1,...,s h_4), and on s=1 Euler reduces this to K=(h_i). The ten-node saturation I has Hilbert function (1,4,10,10,...). An exact Sylvester witness gives H_{R/K}=(1,4,10,16,19,16,10,10,...), so I/K has graded dimensions (6,9,6) and length 21. Degree-4, degree-5, and degree-6 equalities are maximal-rank finite matrix conditions and therefore hold on a nonempty open subset. The local ideals away from P_0 are radical, including (q,su,sv,sw)=(s,q)∩(u,v,w) at each node.

value.rationale: The published cyclic example naturally raises a scheme-theoretic question because rank-locus support does not determine the Jacobian singular scheme. The exact length-21 embedded defect is a structural invariant, not a routine renaming: it distinguishes the actual singular scheme from its reduced quartic-plus-ten-lines support and is relevant to normalization, blowup, deformation, and local singularity calculations. The complete graded defect (6,9,6) explains precisely where saturation fails.
